title: Diagnose poor CB-SEM fit without blindly following modification indices

brief.text: A questionnaire (SYNTHETIC) has eight items. Its authors wrote v1–v4 to measure one facet of the construct and v5–v8 to measure a second facet, but the analyst specified a single factor. Run the starter model with CB-SEM (ML).

SEM Studio does not compute modification indices yet. Suppose a colleague ran the model in lavaan and sends you the largest ones: residual covariances v5~~v6 (MI = 98), v7~~v8 (MI = 85) and v1~~v2 (MI = 71).
brief.title: A colleague's suggestion

tasks.prompt: How do you read the fit of the one-factor model?

options.text: Clearly unacceptable: χ²(20) ≈ 585, RMSEA ≈ .24, CFI ≈ .61, SRMR ≈ .18; the model does not reproduce the covariances.
options.feedback: Correct. Every index points to severe misfit.
No published guideline considers CFI = .61 acceptable.

options.text: Unacceptable only because N = 500 makes χ² sensitive.
options.feedback: RMSEA, CFI and SRMR also signal severe misfit; it is not just a χ² sample-size effect.

options.text: Return to the instrument's design and specify two correlated factors (v1–v4, v5–v8).
options.feedback: Correct. The revision is motivated by theory, not by the indices.

options.text: Free the three suggested residual covariances and re-run.
options.feedback: They would patch symptoms of the missing second factor and capitalise on chance (MacCallum et al. 1992).
Item deletion driven by fit narrows the construct and is not a substantive revision.

tasks.prompt: Respecify the model as the instrument was designed.
Run CB-SEM (ML) on the two-factor model and enter its RMSEA.
tasks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The theoretically specified model fits well.
tasks.feedbackWrong: Not the expected value. Check that each item loads only on its own factor and that the two factors are allowed to correlate.

hints: Compare each index with what you know about typical values, but look at the whole pattern.
Where do the suggested residual covariances lie: within one facet or across facets?
What structure did the questionnaire's authors intend?

solution.text: The one-factor model misfits severely (χ²(20) ≈ 585, RMSEA ≈ .238, CFI ≈ .61, SRMR ≈ .18). The large MIs are all within the item groups v1–v4 and v5–v8: symptoms of a missing second factor. Freeing them would raise fit without explaining anything.

Two correlated factors (v1–v4, v5–v8), as designed, give χ²(19) ≈ 20.5, RMSEA ≈ .013, CFI ≈ .999, SRMR ≈ .025, with a factor correlation of ≈ .29. Report the change and its rationale; ideally confirm on new data.
